landing.metaTitle: NTU Study — Group collaboration for students
landing.metaDesc: Collaborate on courses, projects and reading clubs with shared tasks, flashcards and contribution ratings — built for NTU students.

hero.subtitle: NTU Study brings groups, tasks, files and flashcards into one calm workspace — so your team can focus on the work that matters, and leaders can grade contribution fairly.

features.sectionTitle: The study workspace your group actually opens
features.sectionSubtitle: Stop juggling chat groups, spreadsheets and shared docs. NTU Study replaces the busywork so your team can ship.

groups.title: Study groups, organised
groups.body: Spin up a course or project group, invite classmates with one link, and keep everything in a shared workspace.

tasks.title: Tasks that move
tasks.body: Plan, assign and track work on a Kanban board with sub-tasks, deadlines and automatic reminders.

flashcards.title: Flashcards that stick
flashcards.body: Build decks together and revise with spaced repetition before assessments — no more scattered notes.

contribution.title: Fair contribution scoring
contribution.body: Leaders rate teammates at the end of a project so effort is recognised and free-riding is visible.

records.title: Locked, audit-ready records
records.body: Once a project closes, deliverables and ratings are locked and exportable for academic review.

ntu.title: Made for NTU
ntu.body: Sign in with your NTU Google account. Your groups, files and progress follow you across every module.

howItWorks.sectionTitle: From kickoff to submission, without the chaos

step1.title: Create or join a group
step1.body: Use your NTU Google sign-in and either start a new group or accept an invite link from your leader.

step2.title: Plan and execute
step2.body: Break the project into tasks, attach files, and review flashcards together as the deadline approaches.

step3.title: Lock and rate
step3.body: When the project ends, the leader closes the project. Contribution scores are recorded and exported.

privacy.intro: NTU Study is committed to protecting your personal information. This Privacy Policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, and your rights regarding your information. By using NTU Study, you consent to the data practices described in this policy.
privacy.s1Content: We collect the following types of information: (a) Account information from Google OAuth: your name, email address, and profile picture when you sign in with Google; (b) Usage data: pages visited, features used, and actions taken within the platform; (c) User-generated content: flashcard sets, tasks, group information, and study materials you create; (d) Communication data: invitations sent, group membership, and activity logs.
privacy.s2Content: We use the collected information to: (a) provide and improve our services; (b) authenticate your identity and maintain your account; (c) enable collaboration features such as study groups and shared flashcards; (d) send important notifications about your account and groups; (e) analyze usage patterns to improve the platform; (f) comply with legal obligations.
privacy.s3Content: When you connect Google Drive or Google Calendar, we access only the specific data necessary to provide those features (file storage and calendar events). We do not access your Gmail, contacts, or other Google data not explicitly authorized. You can revoke this access at any time through your Google Account settings at myaccount.google.com.
privacy.s4Content: We do not sell your personal data to third parties. We may share your data only: (a) with other users as required for collaboration features you participate in (e.g., group members can see your display name and profile picture); (b) with service providers who assist us in operating the platform under strict confidentiality agreements; (c) when required by law or to protect legal rights.
privacy.s5Content: Your data is stored on secure servers. We implement industry-standard security measures including encryption in transit (HTTPS/TLS) and at rest, access controls, and regular security reviews. However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, and we cannot guarantee absolute security.
privacy.s6Content: We retain your personal data for as long as your account is active. If you delete your account, we will delete or anonymize your personal information within 30 days, except where retention is required by law or legitimate business purposes (such as resolving disputes).
privacy.s7Content: You have the right to: (a) access the personal data we hold about you; (b) request correction of inaccurate data; (c) request deletion of your account and associated data; (d) export your data in a portable format; (e) withdraw consent for optional data processing. To exercise these rights, contact us at support@ntu-study.app.
privacy.s8Content: NTU Study uses browser localStorage to store your authentication token and language preference. We do not use tracking cookies or third-party advertising cookies. Essential functionality requires localStorage to be enabled in your browser.
privacy.s9Content: NTU Study is not directed at children under 13. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If you believe we have inadvertently collected such information, please contact us immediately and we will delete it.

guide.metaDesc: NTU Study user guide: group collaboration, personal todo list, and flashcards.

hero.subtitle: NTU Study is a collaborative platform built for Nha Trang University students — integrating Google Drive, Canva, group calendars, task management, and flashcards in one place.

groupWorkflow.title: Group Collaboration
groupWorkflow.subtitle: End-to-end guide from creating a group to scoring contributions
groupWorkflow.intro: The NTU Study group workflow consists of 8 sequential steps. Follow the order below to make the most of the platform — from creating a group, assigning tasks, reviewing results, to scoring contributions and locking the project.

createGroup.title: Create a Group
createGroup.subtitle: Initialise your group and auto-provision resources
createGroup.description: When you create a group, the system automatically creates a Google Drive folder, a Canva presentation file, and a shared document — so the whole team is ready to work without any manual setup.
steps: Sign in with your Google account (.edu) → go to Dashboard → click "Create new group".
Enter the group name and description. Set a report date and tags for easy filtering later (optional).
Add member emails at this step if you already have them (optional — you can invite later).
Click "Create group" — the system automatically creates a Drive folder, Canva file, and Google Doc.
After creation, you are redirected to the group page with all resource links visible immediately.
tips: The Leader's Drive storage is used for group resources — check available space before creating if the group will have large files.

inviteMembers.title: Invite Members
inviteMembers.subtitle: Send invites via email or share a link
inviteMembers.description: Leaders have two ways to invite members: send a direct email or generate an invite link to share. When a new member clicks the link, the system automatically creates their account and sends a confirmation email.
steps: Go to the group page → select the "Members" tab.
Click "Invite member" → enter email addresses (one per line, multiple allowed).
Or click "Create invite link" → copy the link → share it via any messaging app.
Members click the link → sign in with Google → account is automatically created and linked to the group.
Leaders see the new member appear in the list as soon as they accept the invitation.
tips: Invite links can expire — if a member reports they cannot join, generate a new link.
Email addresses must be valid; the system will show an error for incorrect formats.

setupResources.title: Set Up Resources
setupResources.subtitle: Manage files, folders, and documents without leaving the app
setupResources.description: The Assets tab lets the whole group manage the Google Drive folder tree without leaving the app — create sub-folders, upload files, preview documents, and track edit history.
steps: Go to the group page → select the "Assets" tab.
Click "Create folder" to add a sub-folder inside the group Drive folder (no special characters in the name).
Click "Upload file" to upload documents — files are saved directly to Drive and appear in the list.
Click any file to preview it inline (supports Office, PDF, and Canva) without downloading.
Switch to the "History" tab to view change logs and comments from Google Drive.
Click the Canva link to edit the group's presentation slide directly in Canva.
tips: Folder names containing / \ : * ? < > | will be rejected — use hyphens or underscores instead.
setupResources.imageAlt: Group file and folder management screen

assignTasks.title: Create & Assign Tasks
assignTasks.subtitle: Delegate work and track each member's progress
assignTasks.description: Both Leaders and members can create group tasks. Group tasks require Leader approval before they are considered complete. The system sends automatic email notifications to the assignee and to the Leader when approval is needed.
steps: Go to the group page → select the "Tasks" tab → click "Create task".
Enter the task content, select the assignee from the member list, and set a due date.
Click "Save" — the system emails the assignee immediately.
(Optional) Open the task → click "Add sub-task" to break it into smaller steps. Sub-tasks have the same features as parent tasks.
Monitor the status board: In Progress / Pending Review / Done to track overall team progress.
tips: A daily cron-job sends reminder emails for overdue tasks — ensuring no one misses a deadline.
assignTasks.imageAlt: Create and assign group tasks screen

calendarEvents.title: Create Calendar Events
calendarEvents.subtitle: Schedule meetings, presentations, and sync with Google Calendar
calendarEvents.description: The Calendar tab lets the group schedule meetings, presentations, and important deadlines. Events are automatically synced to every member's Google Calendar.
steps: Go to the group page → select the "Calendar" tab.
Click a date → select "Create event".
Enter the title, description, start time, and end time.
Click "Save" — the event appears on the group calendar and syncs to all members' Google Calendars automatically.
The system sends reminder emails before each event so no one misses it.
calendarEvents.imageAlt: Group calendar and event creation screen

reviewTasks.title: Submit & Review Tasks
reviewTasks.subtitle: Clear submit → review → pass/fail workflow
reviewTasks.description: When a member finishes their work, they submit the task for Leader review. The Leader can Pass (mark complete) or Fail (return to in-progress for revision). The entire loop is tracked via email notifications.
steps: Member opens an in-progress task → clicks "Submit" — status changes to "Pending Review".
The system emails the Leader with the task details and assignee information.
Leader goes to the "Tasks" tab → filters by "Pending Review" → opens the task to review.
Click "Pass" → task moves to "Done" and the member receives a confirmation email.
Or click "Fail" with a reason note → task returns to "In Progress" and the member is emailed to revise.
Repeat steps 1–4 until the task is passed.
tips: Leaders should add a clear reason when failing a task so the member knows what to fix — avoiding repeated submit cycles.

peerEvaluation.title: Score Contributions
peerEvaluation.subtitle: Anonymous peer evaluation of each member's contribution
peerEvaluation.description: Near the end of the project, the Leader opens a scoring round. Each member anonymously rates all other members from 0–10. Results are only revealed after the deadline passes.
steps: Leader goes to the "Evaluation" tab → clicks "Open evaluation" → sets the scoring deadline.
The system creates an anonymous evaluation form for each group member.
Each member (including the Leader) signs in → goes to "Evaluation" → scores every other member 0–10.
(Optional) Add a written comment to explain the score.
Click "Confirm" to submit — note that each member can only submit once.
After the deadline, the scoring feature is locked. The Leader can view the aggregated results for the whole group.
tips: If a member did not participate, the Leader can mark them as "Not participating" before opening the evaluation round to exclude them.
Scores are completely anonymous — members cannot see who gave them which score.

closeProject.title: Close & Lock Project
closeProject.subtitle: Archive all group data in read-only mode
closeProject.description: When the project is complete, the Leader locks the group. All tasks, documents, and evaluation results are preserved but no one can make further edits — ensuring data integrity.
steps: Leader goes to the group page → selects "Group settings" → clicks "End project".
Confirm the action — the group status changes to "Locked".
All members can still view all group content but cannot create, edit, or delete anything.
Data is stored permanently on the system for future reference.
tips: Locking is irreversible — make sure all tasks have been approved and evaluation scores are finalised before locking.

tasks.title: Personal Todo List
tasks.subtitle: Manage your own tasks, independent of any group
tasks.description: Alongside group tasks, every user has a private personal task space. Create tasks, set deadlines, add sub-tasks, and mark them complete — only you can see and manage these.
steps: Go to Dashboard → select "Personal Todo" → click "Create new task".
Enter the content and due date → click "Save".
Open a task to add sub-tasks if you need to break down the work.
Mark a task complete by clicking its checkbox — the status is saved immediately.
A cron-job automatically sends reminder emails for tasks that are approaching or past their due date.

flashcards.title: Flashcards
flashcards.subtitle: Study and memorise with spaced repetition
flashcards.description: Create personal flashcard decks or share them with your group. The system uses a spaced repetition algorithm to schedule reviews optimally, helping you remember more with less time.
steps: Go to "Flashcards" → click "Create new deck" → enter the deck name and description.
Add cards: enter the front (question) and back (answer) → click "Add card". You can also bulk-import via CSV/Excel.
Click "Start studying" → the system launches a multiple-choice quiz based on cards you haven't mastered yet.
After each question, rate how well you remembered (Easy / Medium / Hard) — the system schedules the next review date automatically.
Leaders can share a deck with the group so all members can study together.
